subject: My simple Hierarchical model is slow and not converging!

messages.author: 3b679b7acf28007c
messages.subject: My simple Hierarchical model is slow and not converging!
parts:
Hi,

I'm fitting a simple hierarchical model and I'm getting some issues (I highlighted one of the issues in the title):

1) First of al, my model is so slow, even if it's a very simple model
2) I tried 2,000 and 5,000, and 10,000 iterations and yet still I have convergence issue.

I thought maybe I could mention my model here so that I get some advice - maybe there is something I'm missing:

data {
  int<lower = 1> N; // number of subjects
  int<lower = 1> Mi; // number of longitudinal measures per subject
  matrix[N, Mi] Y; 
  vector[N] X; // In my data this is binary 0, 1
}
parameters {
  vector[N] beta0_i;
  real<lower = 0> beta1;
  real<lower = 0> sigma_sq;
}
model {
  real meanTmp;
  beta1 ~ normal(0, 10);
  beta0_i ~ normal(0, 10);
    
  log(sigma_sq) ~ normal(-1, 1);
  increment_log_prob(-log(sigma_sq));
  
  for (i in 1:N){
    for (j in 1:Mi){
      meanTmp <- beta0_i[i] + beta1*X[i];
      Y[i,j] ~ normal(meanTmp, sigma_sq);
    }
  }
}

Thanks very much for your help

messages.author: a9e2e9ac319971b0
messages.subject: Re: My simple Hierarchical model is slow and not converging!
parts:
I am not an expert on Stan, but just by looking at your code, one thing I can see which I made same mistake before is that you should vectorize your sampling statement. 
So instead of call Y[i,j] in the loop, you could reshape your model and move it outside of the loop and call Y ~ normal( mean, sigma), it will be must faster this way. 
In the Stan manual, somewhere around page 226-227 have examples on how to vectorize for better speed.

Thanks,

Haoyan

messages.subject: Re: [stan-users] My simple Hierarchical model is slow and not converging!
parts:
Hi, also the scale parameter in the normal is sigma, not sigma_squared.  And if you want a lognormal prior on sigma, you can use lognormal directly rather than the way you did it.
A
